claims.claim: SOURCED: the article asserted in its own voice that an authorization bill authorizes programs but does not itself provide the money. The stored GAO glossary excerpt does not carry the Authorizing Legislation entry and gao.gov still returns HTTP 403 to a browser UA. Bound instead to the bill own official summary and to CRS IF10516, which states it directly.
claims.sourceSpan: Unlike an appropriations bill, the NDAA does not provide budget authority for defense-related activities.
claims.note: Both new authorities are named by the bill summary itself as further reading, which makes them the natural anchor rather than a generic budget glossary.

claims.claim: PARTLY SOURCED, PARTLY REMOVED: the article defined "held at the desk" in its own voice and added that it is "often a placeholder while the two chambers work toward a single, reconciled version." CRS RS22299 supplies a real definition and a real reason set, and neither includes that purpose. The definition is now attributed to CRS and explicitly scoped to Senate practice; the invented purpose clause is DELETED.
claims.sourceSpan: sometimes pending a decision on referring them to committee, passing them without committee consideration, or obtaining clearance from all Senators
claims.section: What Held at the Desk Means
claims.note: RS22299 is scoped to bypassing SENATE committees while our case is the House holding a Senate-passed bill. Stating a chamber-agnostic definition on this authority would be the right-definition-wrong-chamber error, so the article attributes the CRS words to Senate practice and anchors the House side to the S. 2296 action record instead.

claims.claim: CORRECTED: the article said Wicker "pressed to bring it to the floor ahead of a bipartisan amendments agreement that cleared the way for passage." The sequence is the other way round. Roll Call records that the bill had been stalled since early September, that Wicker announced the agreed amendments package on the morning of October 9, and that the votes followed the same day. The article now states the order the source states.
claims.sourceSpan: But on Thursday morning, Senate Armed Services Chairman Roger Wicker, R-Miss., announced that Republicans and Democrats had agreed on an amendments package.
claims.section: Why did supporters back the bill
claims.note: Flagged by the sweep as a U-FLAG; confirmed against the source. The article had the chairman pushing past an agreement he in fact brokered and announced.

claims.claim: REMOVED: "Using an available bill as the vehicle for a negotiated final text is a common end-stage maneuver" was an unsourced frequency claim. No authority read for this audit supports it. CRS IF10516 makes the opposite-direction point - that the NDAA is used as a vehicle FOR other legislation - and using it here would have been a subtle misuse. Deleted and replaced with the sourced record of what S. 1071 actually was and how the House used it.
claims.sourceSpan: 2025-08-01 | Floor | Passed Senate without amendment by Unanimous Consent.
claims.note: The replacement is strictly better content: a Veterans Affairs disinterment bill passed by unanimous consent, held at the House desk for four months, then wholly replaced under a closed rule.

claims.claim: REMOVED: the article said the DEI repeal provisions "drew objection on the floor" with no named holder - an unnamed-collective attribution the site rules forbid. A hostile Congressional Record search found no such objection: the word "diversity" does not appear anywhere in the October 9 passage-day transcript, and a full-text CREC search across the pre-passage window returned only bill-text reprints plus one SUPPORTIVE floor statement, from Wicker. The clause is deleted; Wicker sourced sentence is added in its place and the provisions are now described from the statute text.
claims.sourceSpan: This NDAA supports the DOD's role in border security and rolls back statutory requirements for diversity, equity, and inclusion programs at the Pentagon.
claims.section: Why did supporters back the bill
claims.note: The search could not cover the December S. 1071 window because the shared GovInfo key rate-limited; that gap is recorded in status.md rather than papered over. Nothing in the article now rests on an unnamed objector either way.

claims.claim: CORRECTED - NOT ON THE SWEEP LIST: the article said the December vote "drew the same 77-20 division" and, earlier in the same section, that the Senate agreed "by an identical 77-20 tally." The tally is identical; the division is not. Four senators changed sides - Baldwin (D-WI) and Durbin (D-IL) from no to yes, Bennet (D-CO) and Lee (R-UT) from yes to no - so the December bloc is 17 Democrats, one independent and TWO Republicans, not 18/1/1. Read together with the adjacent sentence naming Paul as the lone Republican no, the article told readers something false about the final vote.
claims.sourceSpan: Lee (R-UT), Nay
claims.note: Found by diffing the two stored roll-call sheets member by member. An identical tally is exactly the kind of coincidence that invites the word "same"; no scripted gate checks whether two equal tallies are the same people.

claims.claim: CORRECTED - NOT ON THE SWEEP LIST: the article said "when LegislationPatch publishes a full analysis of the FY2026 NDAA, it will be linked here." Both analyses have been live for months - 119-S-2296 analysed 2026-08-27 and 119-S-1071 analysed 2026-07-30, each with a static bill page. The promise is replaced with the two links.
claims.note: Identical class to the B1 finding on safe-drugs-act. A frozen article keeps promising something the pipeline has already delivered; nothing in the lane notices.

claims.claim: ADDED - THE B1 LESSON APPLIED: the "What the FY2026 NDAA Authorizes" section was written entirely from the official summary, and that summary is of the bill AS REPORTED on 2025-07-15. The Senate passed S. 2296 with an amendment on 2025-10-09, and the engrossed text runs to TEN divisions - the four the summary describes plus Additional Provisions, the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, Department of State Matters, the Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025, the ROAD to Housing Act and a Department of State Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026. A reader was being shown a four-division bill.
claims.sourceSpan: (9) Division I--ROAD to Housing Act.
claims.note: B1 established that a summary-derived section inherits the summary gaps. This case adds a second axis: the summary was also a VERSION behind, which is worse, because the gap is not an editorial choice by CRS but a bill that changed after the summary was written.

claims.claim: ADDED - NOT ON THE SWEEP LIST: the article described the DEI provisions only as the Senate bill repeals, and never told readers what the enacted law does. Section 901 of Public Law 119-60 is headed PROHIBITION OF DIVERSITY, EQUITY, AND INCLUSION PROGRAMS and, beyond the same repeals, forward-bars a DEI office, a chief diversity officer, DEI plans and surveys, employee resource and affinity groups and DEI or critical-theory training, with a rule of construction preserving EEO and ADA offices. The two texts also differ structurally: ten divisions against eight, and the ROAD to Housing Act is in the Senate bill and nowhere in the law.
claims.sourceSpan: SEC. 901. PROHIBITION OF DIVERSITY, EQUITY, AND INCLUSION PROGRAMS OF THE DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE.
claims.note: The page answers the query "did the defense bill pass" and its own capsule says the NDAA became law under a different number. Describing only the bill that died, on the most-searched provision in it, is the gap this finding closes.

claims.claim: ADDED: the article said "the House takes up its own defense authorization bill" without naming it. CRS IF10516 names H.R. 3838 as the House vehicle and S. 2296 as the Senate one for the 119th Congress, and H.R. 3838 is already analysed in our own corpus.
claims.sourceSpan: Typically, there is a House legislative vehicle (e.g., H.R. 3838 , 119 th Congress)
claims.section: What Held at the Desk Means
claims.note: An unnamed bill is not wrong, but it is unhelpful on a tracker whose whole subject is which vehicle carried the policy.

claims.claim: CORRECTED: the both-sides section said the bill passed "after invoking cloture 84-14" without saying on what. The 84-14 vote was cloture on the MOTION TO PROCEED, five weeks before passage, and the December sequence contained a second and different cloture vote (76-20, Record Vote 647). The article now says which cloture vote it means and when.
claims.sourceSpan: Question: On Cloture on the Motion to Proceed (Motion to Invoke Cloture: Motion to Proceed to S. 2296 )
claims.note: Same class as the KOSA cloture finding: a cloture number quoted without its question.

Bernie Sanders offered an amendment, which failed, to cut the Pentagon budget by 10 percent and redirect the savings to veterans dental care" because nothing cited supported it - correctly, since the Roll Call piece the section rested on mentions Sanders zero times. The claim is nonetheless true. Amendment No. 3853, called up by Sanders on 2025-10-09, was rejected 10-88 on Rollcall Vote No. 568 under a 60-vote threshold. claims.claim: DELIBERATELY NOT USED: two different toplines are available in the stored sources - Wicker on the floor saying the committee adopted "a bill with a $924.7 billion top line", and Roll Call putting the Senate bill at "roughly $914 billion" while noting the figure excludes some national security spending. They are not the same number and neither is the enacted figure. No topline is stated in the article voice.
claims.sourceSpan: we adopted a bill with a $924.7 billion top line
claims.note: Both figures are attributable and could be used with attribution in a later cycle. Publishing either as the topline in the site own voice would be the invented-precision class.

claims.claim: DELIBERATELY NOT NAMED: S. 1071 original title and CRS summary name a deceased private individual whose remains the bill directed the VA to disinter, and the summary carries an unrelated criminal-record detail. The article states the subject matter and cites the roll-call sheet that still carries the old title, without reproducing the name.
claims.sourceSpan: Measure Title: A bill to require the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to disinter the remains
claims.note: The vehicle point - that the NDAA rode a bill about something else entirely - is fully carried by the subject matter. Naming him adds nothing a reader needs and puts a private person on an unrelated indexed page.
